messages.author: d0b18666fe8582cb
messages.subject: output CEs
parts:
Hi Phil,

I hope all is well. I'm wondering if there is an easy way to output the confidence envelope values that are used to plot CEs around the tracelines plotted via itemplot? The reason I ask is that I'm manually plotting my own tracelines using the estimated model probabilities outputted via the probtrace function (doing this manually only because I need to customize the plot a bit more). I'd like to plot CEs as well.

Thank you!
Keri

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: output CEs
parts:
Hi Keri,

There's no easy way to obtain the functions for CEs as these are entirely internal. You could try to reconstruct similar plots using the draw_parameters() function to draw sets of plausible parameters given the ACOV matrix and then following the reasoning detailed in Thissen & Wainer's paper.  

Thissen, D. Wainer, H. Confidence Envelopes for Item Response Theory. Journal of Educational Statistics, 1990, 15, 113-128

Phil

messages.author: 58786c912f9ee9c2
messages.subject: Re: output CEs
parts:
Hi Phil and Keri,

I guess you could consider to extract the values of the envelope from the ggplot object:

data(LSAT7)
fulldata <- expand.table(LSAT7)
mod1 <- mirt(fulldata,1,SE=TRUE)
p <- itemplot(mod1, 2, CE = TRUE)

x <- p$panel.args[[1]]$x
y <- p$panel.args[[1]]$y
u <- p$panel.args.common$upper
l <- p$panel.args.common$lower

plot(x,y, type ="l")
lines(x,u)
lines(x,l)


Kind wishes,
   Philipp
